title: Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations, Part II: Witt vector cohomology of singular varieties
summary: Witt vector cohomology of singular varieties in characteristic p, extending Crystalline cohomology: Witt vector sheaves and their rational and Frobenius-inverted cohomology, Bhatt–Scholze's h-descent, Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault's compactly supported Witt cohomology and its identification with the slope < 1 part of rigid cohomology, Chatzistamatiou–Rülling's action of correspondences on Hodge–Witt cohomology and Witt-rational singularities, and point-count congruences over finite fields: Ax–Katz modulo q, Serre's theta-divisor congruence, and Esnault's theorem for CH_0-trivial and WO-rational varieties.

# Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations, Part II: Witt vector cohomology of singular varieties

**Purpose.** Crystalline cohomology computes the p-adic cohomology of smooth proper varieties in characteristic p, and its slope-[0, 1) part is the Witt vector cohomology H^*(X, WO_X) ⊗ ℚ. This Part II builds Witt vector cohomology as a cohomology theory of *singular* varieties: rational and Frobenius-inverted Witt vector cohomology, its descent for the h-topology (Bhatt–Scholze), compactly supported Witt vector cohomology and its identification with the slope < 1 part of rigid cohomology with compact supports (Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault), the action of algebraic correspondences on relative Hodge–Witt cohomology and Witt-rational singularities (Chatzistamatiou–Rülling), and the resulting congruences for numbers of rational points over finite fields: Ax–Katz modulo q, Serre's theta-divisor congruence, Esnault's theorem that rationally chain connected smooth projective varieties over F_q have a number of rational points congruent to 1 modulo q, and its extension to WO-rational singular varieties used by Gongyo–Nakamura–Tanaka and Hacon–Witaszek.

**Scope and boundaries.** It starts where Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations (CrystallineCohomology) stops: CR.4 owns the de Rham–Witt complex, whose degree-zero part is W_rO, its quasi-coherence and étale descent, the comparison with crystalline cohomology and the slope spectral sequence of smooth proper schemes; CR.0 owns divided power envelopes. Rigid cohomology with and without compact supports, its Frobenius, finiteness, Poincaré duality, proper descent, the Lefschetz trace formula and the rigid–crystalline comparison are imported from P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology, RD.4–RD.7). The h- and v-topologies, abstract blowup squares and the h-descent criterion come from Arc topology and descent (AT.1) and Enhanced derived sheaves (E2); simplicial commutative rings and the simplicial Witt adapter from E5:animation; universal homeomorphisms, Frobenius, coherent duality, Chow groups, refined Gysin maps and de Jong's alterations from Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SF.0–SF.5); Galois alterations from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.6; correspondences of smooth projective varieties from Motives and algebraic cycles (MC.0, MC.2); Riemann–Roch on abelian varieties from Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli (A2). The birational geometry that proves WO-rationality of klt threefolds and fourfolds (minimal model program, flips, dlt modifications) is not here; it imports the definitions and theorems of WV.5 and WV.6.

**Conventions.** p is a prime, k a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K = W[1/p], σ the Frobenius of W. Witt vectors are p-typical (Mathlib's WittVector); F, V, R are Frobenius, Verschiebung and restriction, with FV = VF = p. Two rationalizations are used and never confused: WI_K := WI ⊗ ℚ (tensor convention, used with K-coefficients and compact supports) and WI_ℚ, the image in the Serre localization of sheaves of abelian groups at bounded-torsion sheaves (isogeny convention, used for WO-rationality); R^if_*(WI_ℚ) = 0 means a power of p kills R^if_*(WI). Slopes of F are normalized by v_p(p) = 1; over F_q, slopes of the linear Frobenius φ = F^a by v_q(q) = 1. 'Connected fibres' means connected after every base change to a field-valued point.

**Sources.** Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault, On Witt vector cohomology for singular varieties (Compositio 2007; arXiv:math/0510349); Bhatt–Scholze, Projectivity of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, §§2, 11.5 (Invent. Math. 2017; arXiv:1507.06490); Chatzistamatiou–Rülling, Hodge–Witt cohomology and Witt-rational singularities (Doc. Math. 2012; arXiv:1104.2145), with their earlier Higher direct images of the structure sheaf in positive characteristic (ANT 2011); Gongyo–Nakamura–Tanaka, Rational points on log Fano threefolds over a finite field (JEMS 2019), §2.5–2.6; Nakamura–Tanaka, A Witt Nadel vanishing theorem for threefolds (Compositio 2020), §2.4; Esnault, Varieties over a finite field with trivial Chow group of 0-cycles have a rational point (Invent. Math. 2003); Hacon–Witaszek, On the relative minimal model program for fourfolds in positive and mixed characteristic (Forum Math. Pi 2023), Corollaries 1.3 and 4.7.

**Layers.** WV.0 Witt vector sheaves and rational Witt cohomology; WV.1 h-descent; WV.2 compact supports; WV.3 comparison with rigid cohomology; WV.4 Hodge–Witt cohomology with supports and correspondences; WV.5 Witt-rational singularities; WV.6 point counts and Esnault's theorem.

**Non-goals.** Higher slopes (the full Ax–Katz congruences modulo q^κ for κ > 1 through Witt cohomology), Witt vector cohomology with coefficients, and the minimal model program are outside this roadmap; the convergent log F-isocrystals of Kisin–Madapusi Pera–Shin and the Cartier transforms of Esnault–Groechenig are separate Part IIs of CrystallineCohomology.

stages.title: Witt vector sheaves and rational Witt cohomology
stages.description: Witt vector sheaves W_nO_X, WO_X and Witt ideal sheaves W_nI, WI of a scheme in characteristic p, with R, F, V, Teichmüller and the Witt schemes W_nX; the two rationalizations (tensor with ℚ, and the isogeny category obtained as the Serre localization at bounded-torsion sheaves) with derived direct images on the latter; Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F]. Targets: nil- and radical-invariance of rational Witt sheaves; invariance of Frobenius-inverted and rational Witt cohomology under finite universal homeomorphisms and the connected-fibre criterion WO_{Y,ℚ} ≅ f_*WO_{X,ℚ}; Mayer–Vietoris for closed covers; the higher-direct-image lemmas for W_nI and WI; finiteness and slopes in [0, 1) of H^i(X, WO_X)_K for proper X.

stages.title: h-descent for Frobenius-inverted Witt vector cohomology
stages.description: Fppf descent for Witt vector cohomology; Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology of derived self-products over an affine base equals that of classical self-products; the finite pushout Y′ = Spec(H⁰(X, O_X) ×_{H⁰(E, O_E)} A/J) replacing a blowup square; excision for Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology along abstract blowup squares and all their self-products (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 11.45). Targets: X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] is an h-sheaf on finitely presented schemes over a noetherian F_p-scheme of finite Krull dimension (Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 11.41), and X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/p] is an h-sheaf (Theorem 11.40, the descent of Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault).

stages.title: Witt vector cohomology with compact supports
stages.description: Targets: the vanishing of higher direct images of Witt ideal sheaves along proper maps whose higher direct images of O vanish over the complement of the ideal, uniformly up to a power of p (Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault Theorem 2.4, Chatzistamatiou–Rülling Proposition 4.6.1), and its consequence R^qf_*WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ R^q(f|_E)_*WO_{E,ℚ} through the exceptional locus; Witt vector cohomology with compact supports RΓ_c(U, WO_{U,K}) of a separated k-scheme of finite type, independent of the compactification, contravariant for proper maps, covariant for open immersions, with excision triangles; its finiteness with slopes in [0, 1); proper hypercoverings and simplicial resolutions by smooth quasi-projective schemes; descent for compactly supported Witt cohomology along truncated proper hypercoverings that are étale over a dense open.

stages.title: Comparison with rigid cohomology: the slope < 1 part
stages.description: Slope parts E_λ and E^{<ρ} of F-isocrystals and slope factors of characteristic polynomials; the ring map A_{X,P} → WO_{X,K} from overconvergent functions on a tube defined by a Frobenius lift; the morphism a_U: RΓ_{rig,c}(U/K) → RΓ_c(U, WO_{U,K}), independent of choices, functorial, compatible with excision and equal for smooth proper X to the composite of the rigid–crystalline and crystalline–de Rham–Witt comparisons with the augmentation; simplicial embeddings with Frobenius lifts. Targets: the Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault theorem H^q_{rig,c}(X/K)^{<1} ≅ H^q_c(X, WO_{X,K}) for every separated k-scheme of finite type, and the vanishing of H^i_c(U, WO_{U,K}) for i ≠ dim U when U is smooth affine equidimensional.

stages.title: Hodge–Witt cohomology with supports and the action of correspondences
stages.description: The Witt canonical system W_•ω_X = H^{−d}(W_•(π)^!W_•(k)) with Ekedahl's duality for smooth schemes and the trace for proper maps; the pushforward on Hodge–Witt cohomology with supports along proper maps of smooth schemes (Gros), with f_*f^* = deg f for finite f; Gros's cycle classes as the unique morphism from Chow groups with supports; the category C_S of smooth quasi-projective S-schemes with proper correspondences. Targets: the functor Ĥ(?/S) from C_S to de Rham–Witt modules over S, compatible with F, V, d, with graphs acting by pullback and pushforward (Chatzistamatiou–Rülling Proposition 3.5.4); the vanishing lemmas for correspondences supported in positive codimension.

stages.title: Witt-rational singularities
stages.description: Finite quotients and topological finite quotients; quasi-resolutions and their existence from de Jong's Galois alterations; the projector realizing Witt cohomology of a finite quotient inside that of a smooth cover. Targets: Rf_*WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ WO_{Y,ℚ} and Rf_*Wω_{X,ℚ} ≅ Wω_{Y,ℚ} for a quasi-resolution of a topological finite quotient; WO-rational and Witt-rational singularities, tested on one quasi-resolution; topological finite quotients are Witt-rational and Witt-rationality is invariant under universal homeomorphisms; the Witt singularity complexes WS_{0,S}, WS_{d,S}; quasi-birational invariance of Witt cohomology; rational ⇒ Witt-rational ⇒ WO-rational ⇒ BE-Witt-rational; the criterion for isolated singularities through H^{>0}(E, WO_{E,ℚ}); the Bloch–Srinivas decomposition of the diagonal; vanishing of R^{>0}f_*WO_{X,ℚ} for projective fibrations with universally CH_0-trivial smooth generic fibre (Chatzistamatiou–Rülling Theorem 4.8.1).

stages.title: Point counts modulo q and Esnault's theorem
stages.description: The Witt zeta function ζ^W and slope factors ζ^{<ρ}, with coefficients in ℤ_p; Ax's criterion relating congruences of point counts modulo q^κ to slope factors. Targets: ζ^{<1}(X, t) = ζ^W(X, t) for separated F_q-schemes of finite type; point-count congruences from isomorphisms on Witt cohomology (in particular from isomorphisms on H^i(O)) and for quotients by finite groups; congruences for quasi-birational projective schemes with WO-rational singularities; Witt cohomology of complete intersections of small degree and the Ax–Katz congruence modulo q; Serre's question: two theta divisors of an abelian variety over F_q have congruent point counts modulo q; universally CH_0-trivial and rationally chain connected varieties; Esnault's theorem that H^{>0}(X, WO_X)_ℚ = 0 for universally CH_0-trivial smooth projective X, and |X(F_q)| ≡ 1 mod q for such X and for projective schemes with WO-rational singularities having such a resolution.
